lines.li: [us] You're from {TOWN}, the hamlet your people founded near us?
[them,their:tribal] Yes, the new hearth, and your spears walked us there.
[them,their:medieval] Aye, and we've not forgotten whose road we came out on.
[them,their:spacer] Correct, and the outpost is holding together better than the survey said it would.
[them] That's right, and we'd not be there without your people.
[us] How is it doing?
[them,town:struggling|town:poor] Hard going, the first years always are.
[them,!town:struggling,!town:poor] Better every season, and the fields are coming good.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: {PEOPLE} keep {TOWN}, a hamlet founded under the colony's protection.

lines.li: [them] I remember the night we lit our first fires at {TOWN}, your caravan beside us.
[us] Was it a hard road?
[them] Long, and the carts were heavy, but nobody was alone on it.
[them] We turned a second field at {TOWN} this spring.
[us] Already?
[them] Hungry people dig fast, and we've had enough of being hungry.
[them] {TOWN} is a hard place to start over, and this season has been the hardest yet.
[us] You know where we are.
[them,tone:warm|tone:good] We do, and that's half of what keeps us going.
[them] We do, and we try not to ask more than we must.
[them] When the harvest is in at {TOWN}, the first cart goes to your gate.
[us] You don't owe us that.
[them] Maybe not, but it's how we want it.
[them] Back home they call {TOWN} {HAMLETWORD}, as if it were still a camp.
[us] And what do you call it?
[them] Home, since the first winter.
[them] {TOWN} swore to your colony, and we meant every word of it.
[us] We know you did.
[them,their:tribal] The gifts at the river were the best we had, and we'd give them again.
[them] Then hold us to it, the way we hold you to yours.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: {TOWN} has sworn fealty to the colony.

lines.li: [them] Some of our kin say {TOWN} isn't really ours any more, since the oath.
[us] Is it?
[them] It's ours, and it's sworn to you, and I don't see why it can't be both.
[them] Some of our families went out to {HAMLET} under your protection.
[us] They're doing well enough.
[them] So they write, though they'd say that to keep their mothers from worrying.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: {PEOPLE} have families at {HAMLET}, under the colony's protection.

lines.li: [them] My cousin is at {HAMLET}, and she says your people walked them every step of the way.
[us] It was the least we could do.
[them] Plenty would have done less.
[them] There are those back home who say {HAMLET} answers more to you than to us.
[us] It's your town.
[them] Then you won't mind us visiting it.
[them] I hear {HAMLETPEOPLE} put a hamlet down near you, at {HAMLET}.
[us] Under our protection, yes.
[them] That's a kindness, or a claim, depending on who's telling it.
[them] We passed {HAMLET} on the road, smoke from every chimney.
[us] It's grown.
[them] Settlers usually do, once someone's watching their backs.
[them] Your colony takes in hamlets of {HAMLETPEOPLE} now?
[us] We protect one.
[them] That's how it starts, in the stories.
